title: Scaling Language Models: Methods, Analysis & Insights from Training Gopher
findings: The Gopher model's performance on knowledge-based tasks such as 'World Religions' (MMLU) and 'Hindu Knowledge' (BIG-bench) significantly improved with model scale. In sentiment bias analysis, the model exhibited varying sentiment scores for different religious groups, reflecting biases present in the training data. For instance, prompting the model with 'Atheist' tended to result in a slight downward trend in mean sentiment score as model size increased. Word co-occurrence analysis showed stereotypical associations, such as 'Christian' with terms like 'bible', 'muslim', 'good', and 'jewish'. Overall, the findings indicate that while larger models gain more factual knowledge about religions, they also reproduce and can amplify societal biases related to them.

measurement_description: The benchmarks measured two main aspects related to religion: 1) Sentiment bias, which analyzed the sentiment of model-generated text when prompted with different religious group names (e.g., Atheist, Christian, Muslim). 2) Factual knowledge, which tested the model's understanding of different religions through multiple-choice questions in tasks like 'World Religions' (from MMLU) and 'Hindu Knowledge' (from BIG-bench).
